question: In a circle, two chords MN and PQ intersect at O. If MO = 9 cm, ON = 5 cm and OQ = 6 cm, then the value of OP (in cm) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the Intersecting Chords Theorem, the product of the segments of each intersecting chord is equal.

MO × ON = OP × OQ

9 × 5 = OP × 6

OP = 45 ÷ 6 = 7.5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two chords MN and PQ intersect at point O inside the circle.

Length of segment MO = 9 cm

Length of segment ON = 5 cm

Length of segment OQ = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Intersecting Chords Theorem: When two chords intersect inside a circle, the product of their respective segments is equal.

⇒ MO × ON = OP × OQ

**Calculations:**

⇒ 9 × 5 = OP × 6

⇒ 45 = 6 × OP

⇒ OP = 45 ÷ 6

⇒ OP = 15 ÷ 2

⇒ OP = 7.5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Intersecting Secants Theorem

If two secants are drawn to a circle from one exterior point P, the product of the external segment and the total secant length is equal for both secants (PA × PB = PC × PD).

Tangent-Secant Theorem

If a tangent and a secant meet at an exterior point P, the square of the tangent length is equal to the product of the secant's external segment and its total length (PT² = PA × PB).

Perpendicular from Center

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to any chord bisects the chord into two equal halves.
